definitions.gloss: to take lightly; to underestimate; to not take seriously
definitions.explanation: To fail to recognize the difficulty or seriousness of something, or to look down on someone's ability. A common idiomatic expression used as a warning or criticism.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}を{甘|あま}く{見|み}ていた。
{自然|しぜん}の{力|ちから}を{甘|あま}く{見|み}てはいけない。
examples.english: You must not underestimate the power of nature.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}を{甘|あま}く{見|み}たばかりに、{大|おお}きな{失敗|しっぱい}をしてしまった。
examples.english: Because I underestimated the opponent, I made a big mistake.

notes:
USAGE:
{甘|あま}く{見|み}る is an extremely common expression in everyday Japanese. It is often used in the negative imperative form {甘|あま}く{見|み}るな or {甘|あま}く{見|み}てはいけない to warn someone not to be complacent. The past form {甘|あま}く{見|み}ていた implies regret for having been careless.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜を{甘|あま}く{見|み}る (to underestimate ~)
- {甘|あま}く{見|み}るな (don't underestimate)
- {甘|あま}く{見|み}てはいけない (you must not take lightly)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {侮|あなど}る: to look down on, to scorn
- {軽|かろ}んじる: to make light of (formal)
- なめる: to look down on (very colloquial, rough)
